newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco documents set for release in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco documents set for release in Florida.

text.p: A Florida judge Wednesday ordered the immediate release of eight secret tobacco company documents that the cigarette makers had fought to keep secret for more than a year.

Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen ruled in Florida's lawsuit against the tobacco companies after the state's 4th District Court of Appeal refused late Tuesday to rehear a request to keep the papers secret.
The appeals court also rejected any attempt by the tobacco industry to seek further review before the Florida Supreme court, which is in recess until August 18.
The appeals court has the right to prohibit appeals when it deems that no consititutional issue is involved and the court said that this issue does not pertain to any constitutional right.

The tobacco companies had argued that the documents were protected by attorney-client privilege. But the appeals court agreed with Cohen that they were exempt from that privilege because they involved alleged plans to commit a crime or fraud.
An attorney for Philip Morris Cos Inc, Peter Bleakley, said after Cohen's ruling that "We intend no further appeals on this matter."
The documents from the Brooke Group Ltd's Ligget Group were expected to be released by midday Wednesday. They include company research pertaining to the health effects of smoking.

Jury selection began Friday on Florida's lawsuit, which accuses cigarette makers of misleading the public about the health risk of smoking. The state is seeking to recover public money spent to treat tobacco-related illnesses.
